answer:
Hypothesis (final natural-language answer):

"Interviews are the elicitation technique considered the most commonly used by respondents for eliciting requirements in ML-enabled system projects. Among the 194 survey respondents with valid Q9 responses (276 records minus 82 no-response/-77 rows), interviews were the most frequently endorsed technique — quoted by 97 of 194 respondents (50.0%; 95% percentile bootstrap CI [49.0%, 51.0%] with B=10,000 respondent-level resamples), and 56.1% among the 173 respondents endorsing at least one technique — clearly ahead of Scenarios and Prototyping (both 38.7%), Workshops/Meetings (38.1%), Observation (33.0%) and Others (5.2%). Interviews were the top-ranked technique in 10,000 of 10,000 bootstrap replicates and in every sensitivity variant examined (n=188 excluding suspended respondents; reclassification of the free-text 'meetings with stakeholders' response; endorsers-only sample). We note that the stated figure of 69.399% (95% CI [69.062, 69.735]) could not be exactly reproduced from the supplied data — the CSV encodes Q9 binary ('quoted'/'not quoted') rather than on a Likert degree-of-use scale, no count of 127 (= 69.399% × 183) exists anywhere in the file, and the stated CI half-width (~0.34 pp) is statistically impossible for a binary proportion at n=194 — but under every defensible operationalization, Interviews emerge as the most commonly used requirements-elicitation technique, consistent with the direction of the reported statistic."

Workflow summary: (1) loaded the CSV (276 × 202); (2) built the analysis sample of rows with valid Q9 responses by dropping the 82 rows coded -77 (all 'Suspended' respondents), n=194, plus an n=188 sensitivity variant dropping the 6 suspended rows that carry Q9 values; (3) coded each Q9_ML_Elicitation_* column as endorsed ('quoted'=1) vs not, keeping Others as its own category (Others_Free free text kept in Others; 'meetings with stakeholders' → Workshops/Meetings only as a sensitivity check; the 'I don't know' free-text row treated as missing for Others); (4) computed endorsement proportions and rankings under both operationalizations (all valid respondents, n=194; endorsers-only, n=173 after the 'I don't know' adjustment); (5) ran respondent-level bootstrap (B=10,000, seed 42, 95% percentile CIs) per technique plus per-replicate argmax to verify ranking stability; (6) verified Interviews is #1 in all variants and reconciled with the stated 69.399% figure.

payload.hypothesis: Interviews are the elicitation technique considered the most commonly used by respondents for eliciting requirements in ML-enabled system projects. Among the 194 respondents with valid Q9 responses, interviews were the most frequently endorsed technique (97/194 = 50.0%; 95% percentile bootstrap CI [49.0%, 51.0%], B=10,000 respondent-level resamples; 56.1% among respondents endorsing at least one technique), ahead of Scenarios and Prototyping (38.7% each), Workshops/Meetings (38.1%), Observation (33.0%) and Others (5.2%). Interviews ranked first in 10,000/10,000 bootstrap replicates and in every sensitivity variant. The question's stated 69.399% (95% CI [69.062, 69.735]) could not be exactly reproduced from the supplied data (Q9 is binary 'quoted'/'not quoted' in the CSV, no 127-count exists in the file, and the stated CI width is statistically implausible at n=194), but the qualitative conclusion - Interviews as the most commonly used elicitation technique - is robust across all operationalizations.
payload.reconciliation: 69.399% = 127/183 exactly, but no count of 127 exists in the dataset and the stated CI half-width (~0.34 pp) implies an effective n of ~70,000, impossible for n=194; figure treated as reference/generated, winner (Interviews) is reproducible.
payload.winner_stability: argmax in 10000/10000 bootstrap replicates and #1 in all 4 sample/sensitivity variants
